p: Explain the first assignment or condition that determines the output.
Explain why a star usually needs fewer physical links.
code_first.a: 10; 6; five-node star normally has four peripheral links to central switch.

original_exam_questions: State what a switch does in a LAN. [2 marks]
Forwards frames to the appropriate device/port using learned MAC address information.
Give the purpose of a router. [2 marks]
Connects separate networks and forwards packets between them using IP routing.
Calculate full-mesh connections for four nodes. [2 marks]

optional_original_challenge.coreHint: For n full-mesh nodes, use n×(n−1) DIV 2.

stretch.task: Calculate mesh links for six nodes and compare with a six-device star.
stretch.hint: A star has one link from each device to a central switch.
stretch.answer: Full mesh: 6×5÷2=15; six peripherals in a star use six links to the switch.

mastery.task: Design a loop that tabulates full-mesh and star link counts for n=2 to 8 and identifies where the mesh needs at least twice as many.
mastery.hint: Compute both values on each iteration and compare.
mastery.answer: If n is number of peripheral/device nodes: mesh n(n−1)/2, star n; mesh≥2×star from n≥5. State star counting assumption.
